t: You're looking at Bankside Power Station, the huge former power plant on the south bank of the Thames, which has housed the Tate Modern art museum since 2000. It generated electricity from 1891 to 1981, and was also a training base for apprentices from all over the country. The building was designed by Giles Gilbert Scott, the architect also known for Battersea Power Station and for designing the iconic red telephone box. His hand is why this industrial building now works so well as a gallery.
